ai.description: *Polypedates bengalensis* is a 5–7 cm tree frog with a tan to brown dorsum featuring dark brown blotches. It is distinguished by a dark lateral stripe and translucent, unpigmented webbing on the feet.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Polypedates bengalensis* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, dark brown hourglass-shaped marking on its dorsum, which is absent in similar congeners.
ai.habitat: *Polypedates bengalensis* typically inhabits tropical moist deciduous forests and human-altered landscapes, often found in vegetation near water bodies at low to moderate altitudes.
ai.behavior: The Brown Blotched Bengal Tree Frog is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for insects among vegetation near water bodies.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Polypedates bengalensis* is an egg-laying species that breeds during the monsoon (June–August), depositing clutches of 100–200 eggs within foam nests on vegetation.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Polypedates bengalensis* is found in the West Bengal state of India, specifically within the lower Gangetic plains at low elevations.
ai.callDescription: The Brown Blotched Bengal Tree Frog emits a series of rapid, high-pitched "tuck-tuck" notes, typically heard near stagnant water bodies or monsoon-filled ditches.
